builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
summary: Model Carving replaces fixed, uniform Transformer topologies by learning scalar gates on each attention and MLP sublayer so that training itself removes components, substituting post-hoc pruning or distillation pipelines with a single joint weight-and-architecture run. It costs an extra gating mechanism and training procedure integrated into pretraining from scratch, which the paper validates at 140M–2.7B parameters, a compute budget incompatible with one 24 GB GPU; inference afterwards is cheaper, but producing the carved model is not. It can fail if gate learning collapses to suboptimal topologies for a given task, if the heterogeneous sparse structure does not map to real hardware speedups outside the paper's setup, or if the claimed gains do not transfer when applied to fine-tuning existing checkpoints rather than full pretraining.
rationale: The technique is validated only through from-scratch pretraining at 140M–2.7B scale, which exceeds the reader's single-GPU budget, so it is relevant to track but not adoptable now.
technique: Learnable sublayer gating for architecture pruning during pretraining

claims.statement: Model Carving replaces fixed, uniform Transformer topologies by learning scalar gates on each attention and MLP sublayer so that training itself removes components, substituting post-hoc pruning or distillation pipelines with a single joint weight-and-architecture run. It costs an extra gating mechanism and training procedure integrated into pretraining from scratch, which the paper validates at 140M–2.7B parameters, a compute budget incompatible with one 24 GB GPU; inference afterwards is cheaper, but producing the carved model is not. It can fail if gate learning collapses to suboptimal topologies for a given task, if the heterogeneous sparse structure does not map to real hardware speedups outside the paper's setup, or if the claimed gains do not transfer when applied to fine-tuning existing checkpoints rather than full pretraining.
Carved models match the validation loss of dense models trained with up to 1.7x more compute, and run with up to 34% fewer FLOPs per token and 1.6x faster decoding.
